pr_title: Fix date parsing template int in history stats
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Templates now can render native types. With the `history_stats` you can specify an start/end date using a template. The template result is parsed, however, you can't `parse_datetime` on a integer.

This PR adds a guard for that.

Originally, the `start` was fixed as part of #41227, however, the `end` was missed. Nevertheless, now it only tries parsing if the value is actually a string, else don't even bother.

issue_context.title: History_stats error 0.117.0.dev20201007: int instead of str
issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
The history_stats component complains since 0.117.0.dev20201007 about the end value. To should be str instead of int.
I tried with several datetime conversion filter, but nothing resolved my issue....

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->
Raspi4 docker container

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.117.0.dev20201007
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 0.117.0.dev20201006
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): Container ARM RASPI4
- Integration causing this issue: history_stats
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/history_stats/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```
- platform: history_stats
  name: heizung_warmwasser_between_5_and_23
  entity_id: binary_sensor.heizung_warmwasser
  state: 'on'
  type: ratio
#23 Uhr gestern (Warmwasser Nachtschaltung Start)
  end: '{{ ((as_timestamp(now().replace(hour=0).replace(minute=0).replace(second=0))|int) - 3600) }}'
  duration:
#5 Uhr morgens (Warmwasser Nachschaltung Ende)
    hours: 18
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```
Update for sensor.heizung_warmwasser_between_5_and_23 fails
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 278, in async_update_ha_state
    await self.async_device_update()
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 474, in async_device_update
    raise exc
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/concurrent/futures/thread.py", line 57, in run
    result = self.fn(*self.args, **self.kwargs)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/history_stats/sensor.py", line 197, in update
    self.update_period()
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/history_stats/sensor.py", line 293, in update_period
    end = dt_util.parse_datetime(end_rendered)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/util/dt.py", line 127, in parse_datetime
    return ciso8601.parse_datetime(dt_str)
TypeError: argument 1 must be str, not int
```

## Additional information
comments:
Dear @frenck 
could it be related to Add native Python types support to templates (#41227)?
Here the start was changed to: 
````
dt_util.parse_datetime(str(start_rendered))
````
while the end wasn't touched:             
````
dt_util.parse_datetime(end_rendered)
````

Hey there @phracturedblue, @tetienne, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`template`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L443) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Just for fun, can you try this to see if it produces the same error?

```
  end: '{{ now().replace(hour=0).replace(minute=0).replace(second=0) - timedelta(hours=1) }}'
```

Dear @tdejneka 
i will check that too. 
Yesterday I temp. changed the history_stats/sensor.py code line 293 from:
dt_util.parse_datetime(end_rendered)
to
dt_util.parse_datetime(str(end_rendered))
That fixed the error message in the log file!
But it seems to be that my calculation doens't reflect UTC/CET differences (this is another story)...
yes, this is related to #41227. Thanks for reporting, will look into this.

Dear @tdejneka
i have tested your approach (which is definitely the better one) with my patched sensor.py version - it works. I will retest it with the next dev built again. 
Thanks to all of you all for your qualified feedback and fast reaction!

review_comments: If it's not a string, we should throw an error and return. Or else it will fail on line 309. Same for end.

If it is not a string, it will try the approach directly below this one (which is timestamp based), which throws the error in that case.

In case nothing works, it will never reach line 309.
